title: Why he stayed 28 years: Duke kept updating the repertoire
summary: Duke made some fifteen different arrangements of Solitude and other hits, so playing them never went stale.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Duke Ellington kept his band and his music up to date. Now, like I was telling some people last night, Duke, he listened to a -- for instance, we have certain tunes which are popular, like take, "Solitude," for instance. During the time I was in the band Duke must have made 15 different arrangements on, "Solitude," on, "Sophisticated Lady," "Mood Indigo," those type of things which were popular and which he had many, many requests for.
He'd bring them up to date. Kept updating them all the time. So naturally they didn't become stagnant to the band. And Duke's whole repertoire changed and

changed and changed. And if you -- so for instance, after I was in the band 10 years, I could look back on -- and also listen to the recordings, what we played then. And after I was in the band 15 years I could look back and see, and I'd say, "Oh, did I do that? Oh, that's terrible. Did I play that? Oh." You know, right up to the last. So that didn't -- it wasn't that way.
